football_evidence.question: Can Florida Atlantic contain UTSA’s explosive runs?
football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward UTSA, and its own breakdown accounts for about 0.0 of the 3.2 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.
supporting: When Florida Atlantic has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Florida Atlantic’s offense has allowed a sack on 5.2% of its dropbacks, and UTSA’s defense sacks the quarterback on 9.0% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).

When Florida Atlantic has the ball (big plays on the ground): Florida Atlantic’s offense turns 4.5% of its runs into explosive gains, and UTSA’s defense gives up explosive gains on 4.7% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).

When UTSA has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): UTSA’s offense has allowed a sack on 3.9% of its dropbacks, and Florida Atlantic’s defense sacks the quarterback on 4.6% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).
When UTSA has the ball (the run game against the run defense): UTSA’s offense averages 5.4 yards per carry, and Florida Atlantic’s defense allows 7.3 yards per carry (FBS average 5.0).
contradicting: When Florida Atlantic has the ball (third down): Florida Atlantic’s offense converts 52.1% of its third downs, and UTSA’s defense allows opponents to convert 38.8% of their third downs (FBS average 39.6%).

Caden Veltkamp has completed 229 of 316 passes (72.5%) for 2,633 yards, 8.3 yards per attempt, 24 touchdowns and 4 interceptions in eight games for Florida Atlantic, and has been sacked on 15 of 331 dropbacks.

Owen McCown has completed 167 of 240 passes (69.6%) for 1,738 yards, 7.2 yards per attempt, 11 touchdowns and 4 interceptions in eight games for UTSA, and has been sacked on 10 of 250 dropbacks.
